messages.content: "請您進行一個統計t檢定，以檢查兩個獨立數據集的平均值是否有統計上的差異？第一個數據集，數據集A，包含以下整數：12、15、18、20、22、25、28、30、32、35。第二個數據集，數據集B，包含以下整數：14、17、19、21、23、26、29、31、33、36。請分別以顯著性水平0.05和0.01進行兩次檢定。"

function.name: t_test
function.description: Perform a statistical t-test to check if the means of two independent datasets are statistically different. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

alpha.description: Significance level for the test. Default is 0.05. This is a float type value.

message.reasoning:
We need to perform t-test on two independent samples. We have dataset A: [12,15,18,20,22,25,28,30,32,35] (10 values). Dataset B: [14,17,19,21,23,26,29,31,33,36] (10 values). We need to compute t-statistic and p-value for alpha=0.05 and alpha=0.01. Use two-sample t-test assuming equal variances? Usually t-test for independent samples with equal variances (pooled). But we can also do Welch's t-test. The problem didn't specify. We'll assume equal variances. Compute means, variances, pooled variance, t-statistic, degrees of freedom = n1+n2-2 = 18. Then compute two-tailed p-value. Let's compute.

Dataset A: sum = 12+15+18+20+22+25+28+30+32+35 = let's sum: 12+15=27, +18=45, +20=65, +22=87, +25=112, +28=140, +30=170, +32=202, +35=237. So mean_A = 237/10 = 23.7.

Compute sum of squares: compute each deviation squared.

A deviations from mean 23.7:
12: -11.7 -> sq 136.89
15: -8.7 -> 75.69
18: -5.7 -> 32.49
20: -3.7 -> 13.69
22: -1.7 -> 2.89
25: 1.3 -> 1.69
28: 4.3 -> 18.49
30: 6.3 -> 39.69
32: 8.3 -> 68.89
35: 11.3 -> 127.69

Sum of squares: 136.89+75.69=212.58; +32.49=245.07; +13.69=258.76; +2.89=261.65; +1.69=263.34; +18.49=281.83; +39.69=321.52; +68.89=390.41; +127.69=518.10. So sum of squared deviations = 518.10. Sample variance s1^2 = 518.10/(n1-1)=518.10/9=57.5667.

Dataset B: values: 14,17,19,21,23,26,29,31,33,36. Sum: 14+17=31, +19=50, +21=71, +23=94, +26=120, +29=149, +31=180, +33=213, +36=249. Mean_B = 249/10 = 24.9.

Deviations:
14: -10.9 -> 118.81
17: -7.9 -> 62.41
19: -5.9 -> 34.81
21: -3.9 -> 15.21
23: -1.9 -> 3.61
26: 1.1 -> 1.21
29: 4.1 -> 16.81
31: 6.1 -> 37.21
33: 8.1 -> 65.61
36: 11.1 -> 123.21

Sum squares: 118.81+62.41=181.22; +34.81=216.03; +15.21=231.24; +3.61=234.85; +1.21=236.06; +16.81=252.87; +37.21=290.08; +65.61=355.69; +123.21=478.90. So sum of squared deviations = 478.90. Sample variance s2^2 = 478.90/9 = 53.2111.

Pooled variance sp^2 = ((n1-1)*s1^2 + (n2-1)*s2^2)/(n1+n2-2) = (9*57.5667 + 9*53.2111)/18 = (518.1003 + 478.8999)/18 = 997.0002/18 = 55.38999. So sp^2 ≈ 55.39. Standard error of difference: sqrt(sp^2*(1/n1 + 1/n2)) = sqrt(55.39*(0.1+0.1)) = sqrt(55.39*0.2) = sqrt(11.078) = 3.328. t-statistic = (mean_A - mean_B)/SE = (23.7-24.9)/3.328 = (-1.2)/3.328 = -0.3607. Absolute t = 0.3607.

Degrees of freedom df=18. Two-tailed p-value: For t=0.3607, df=18. Use t distribution. Roughly p ~ 0.72? Let's approximate: t=0.36 is small. For df=18, t critical for alpha=0.05 two-tailed is about 2.101. For alpha=0.01 two-tailed is about 2.878. Our t is far less than critical, so fail to reject null. p-value > 0.7. Let's compute more precisely: Use t cumulative distribution. For t=0.3607, df=18. The two-tailed p = 2*(1 - CDF(|t|)). For small t, CDF ~ 0.64? Actually for t=0.36, CDF maybe ~0.64? Let's approximate using t distribution table: For df=18, t=0.3607, the one-tailed probability maybe ~0.36? Wait, t=0.36 is small, so probability of t <= 0.36 is about 0.64? Actually for normal distribution, z=0.36 gives CDF ~0.640. For t with df=18, similar. So one-tailed p ~ 0.64. Two-tailed p ~ 1.28? That can't be >1. Wait, we need 2*(1-CDF). If CDF ~0.64, then 1-CDF ~0.36, times 2 = 0.72. So p ~0.72. Good.

Thus p-value ~0.72. So at alpha=0.05 and 0.01, we fail to reject null. Provide results.
